summary_of_change:
Across the trailing four quarters (Q3 2025 through Q2 2026), Vistra has demonstrated strong operational execution across its integrated portfolio of 38,700 MW of generation capacity and ~4.3 million retail customer accounts. Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA grew 30.8% YoY in Q2 2026 to $1,767 million, building on Q1 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $1,494 million and full-year 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of $5,912 million. Management has reaffirmed full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6.8B–$7.6B and Adjusted FCFbG of $3.925B–$4.725B, underpinned by ~100% hedge coverage for 2026 and ~94% for 2027.

Operational momentum is reinforced by major strategic transactions: closing the 2,600 MW Lotus gas acquisition in late 2025, announcing the $4.0B net purchase of the 5,500 MW Cogentrix gas fleet (targeting mid-to-late 2026 close), securing long-term nuclear PPAs with Amazon Web Services (up to 1,200 MW at Comanche Peak) and Meta (PJM fleet uprates/renewals), and launching the Helix Digital Infrastructure JV with KKR and NVIDIA. Balance sheet strength has been formally validated by credit upgrades to Investment Grade (BBB-/Baa3) from both S&P and Fitch.

market_pricing_in:
At $137.15, the market is pricing Vistra Corp. ($VST) as a premier infrastructure winner of the artificial intelligence datacenter boom. Trading at 18.4x P/OE and 24.4x EV/OE, VST commands a significant premium over traditional independent power producers (IPPs). Investors are treating Vistra's dispatchable generation footprint—specifically its 6.4 GW nuclear baseload fleet and strategic ERCOT/PJM natural gas power assets—as essential, speed-to-power infrastructure capable of fetching long-duration, high-margin bilateral Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with hyperscalers.

However, this valuation framework assumes that elevated wholesale spark spreads and tight capacity auction clears (such as PJM's record ~$329/MW-day pricing) are permanent features of the grid rather than mid-cycle cyclical peaks. Bears emphasize that beneath the AI narrative lies a business still exposed to commodity volatility, severe ERCOT forward curve softening, retail customer volume decay (including a 7.8% YoY drop in Texas retail volumes), and multi-billion-dollar GAAP net income swings driven by unrealized mark-to-market (MTM) derivative hedging positions.
why_it_might_be_right:
1. Starting Baseline: State starting normalized Owner Earnings of $7.47/share ($2,543.1M total) and net balance sheet cash/debt of $-45.27/share ($-15,415M total).

2. Forensic Business Headwinds: Identify key structural vulnerabilities including severe ERCOT forward curve softening, retail customer attrition (especially the 7.8% YoY decline in Texas retail sales volumes), and massive non-cash derivative hedging losses ($472M unrealized MTM loss in Q2 2026) that drag down GAAP earnings.

3. Skeptic Unit Contraction: Model a downside scenario where retail customer accounts contract from 4.3 million to 3.9 million, and realized wholesale energy pricing declines due to rapid solar and battery storage additions in ERCOT, reducing annualized revenue to $13,500.0M by Year 3.

4. Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation: Deduct sticky cash operating expenses and maintenance CapEx from the degraded revenue, resulting in a compressed Owner Cash Margin of 13.9%, which yields a degraded Skeptic Year-3 Owner Earnings of $5.50/share ($1,872.7M total).

5. Downside Risk Valuation Floor: Capitalize the degraded $5.50/share at a conservative trough multiple of 8.0x P/OE (reflecting a stagnant or contracting business) and add the ending net cash of $-36.46/share (reflecting starting debt partially offset by $3,000M in cumulative net cash generation) to derive a Downside Floor Target of $7.54/share.

what_if_it_keeps_going_that_way:
1. Starting Unit Baseline: State exact starting volume units of 38,700 MW generation capacity and ~4.3 million retail electricity/gas customer accounts across ERCOT, PJM, and CAISO, with monetization driven by realized energy and capacity wholesale pricing ($/MWh) and retail contract margin yields, establishing an annualized revenue run-rate of $16,068.0M.

2. 3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation: Project volume units across the next 3 years, assuming generation capacity expands to 44,200 MW by Year 3 to reflect the integration of the 5,500 MW Cogentrix acquisition, while retail customer accounts experience minor competitive churn, stabilizing at 4.2 million accounts.

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue (Units × Monetization): Multiply the expanded Year 3 generation capacity and stabilized retail accounts by projected monetization yields (incorporating higher PJM capacity auction clears at ~$329/MW-day and stable retail margins) to derive a Projected Year 3 Revenue of $18,500.0M.

4. Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings: Subtract cash operating expenses, including COGS, SG&A, maintenance CapEx of $1,994.0M, and stock-based compensation of $85.0M, to derive a Projected Year 3 Total Owner Earnings of $4,086.0M, representing an Owner Cash Margin of 22.1% and $12.00/share based on 340.5 million outstanding shares.

5. Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge: Calculate the ending balance sheet position starting from Net Cash of $-15,415M, adding cumulative 3-year free cash flow of $11,000M, subtracting $0.0M in share buybacks (strictly adhering to the mandate of zero buybacks due to negative starting net cash), and subtracting $1,500M in growth CapEx, resulting in an Ending Year 3 Net Cash of $-5,915M, or $-17.37/share.

6. Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return: Project a Year 3 Owner Earnings YoY growth rate of 10.5% (g₃). Applying a 2-Factor Exit Multiple of 13.5x P/OE from the Narrow Moat "Steady Compounding" matrix yields a capitalized value of $162.00/share ($12.00/share × 13.5x). Adding the Ending Year 3 Net Cash of $-17.37/share results in an Intrinsic Fair Value Target of $144.63 per share, delivering an expected 3-year annualized return (IRR) of 1.78% from today's market price of $137.15.
